aspect: The composition of the card base
description: Roughly 120 million active payment cards per CBN and NIBSS metrics, of which about 95% are standard naira debit cards linked to consumer naira accounts - the exact cards that faced the $20 monthly international ceiling and blanket suspensions. Many fintech-issued cards were built entirely on domestic rails with no international capability at all.
energy_note: A hundred and twenty million cards, and a twenty-dollar ceiling.

description: A software subscription, a conference registration, an exam fee, a domain renewal, a textbook, a visa application portal. The ceiling is below the price of participating in a professional life.
energy_note: Priced out of the internet by your own bank card.

description: Many banks disable international online payments unless explicitly enabled, and the setting often resets after a few days or a number of transactions - so a card that worked last month declines at checkout with no explanation.
energy_note: It worked in March. It does not work in April.

aspect: And the merchant may have blocked the BIN anyway
description: Merchants and processors maintain BIN blocklists by issuing country as fraud prevention, so a fully functional card can still be declined because the merchant has decided not to accept cards from that bank.
energy_note: Declined by a shop, for your bank's first six digits.

description: Her professional certification exam costs $215. Her card ceiling is $20. She pays a man in a WhatsApp group 12% to put it on his UK card, sends him the naira, and trusts him, because the alternative is not sitting the exam.
money_note: The 12% premium on an unavoidable payment.
energy_note: Paying a stranger a commission to be allowed to take an exam.
